title: Why You Shouldn't Share Your Views With Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that teachers should keep their personal political and social views out of the classroom entirely, not because those views are necessarily wrong, but because doing otherwise wastes limited instructional time that students desperately need. He frames the teacher's real obligation around three focus areas: deep content expertise, strong behavioral accountability, and physical and emotional safety, arguing each of these does more for students than any amount of shared opinion. The piece is sharply critical of declining accountability in schools, describing it as connected to a decline in kindness, empathy, and respect, and insists teachers must be tough-minded enough to make hard calls despite student pushback or difficult home circumstances. He distinguishes being a leader and role model from being a peer or friend who shares personal beliefs, arguing students need expertise and structure, not a teacher's politics. The article closes with a call to protect instructional time and students' wellbeing by staying focused on teaching rather than persuasion.
points: Teachers should avoid sharing personal political or social views in class primarily because doing so wastes instructional time students urgently need.
The teacher's real job centers on three areas: deep content expertise, strong behavioral accountability, and physical and emotional safety.
Declining accountability in schools is linked to a broader erosion of kindness, empathy, and respect among students.
Teachers must be tough-minded enough to make hard, unpopular decisions for students' benefit, even amid difficult home circumstances or pushback.
A teacher's role is to be a leader and role model who imparts skill and knowledge, not a peer who shares personal opinions or politics.
quotes: But it’s a mistake. It’s a mistake not only because your views are just your views, but more importantly, you don’t have time . Education is their way out.
Accountability in school is dying, and with it goes kindness, empathy, respect, and politeness. The behavior of students without accountability is growing more alarming by the day.

To be an effective teacher today, you must be tough-minded. You must care enough for your students to make the hard decisions. You must do the right thing for them even if they don’t understand in the moment.
But you’re not a friend. You’re not a cool youthful semi-adult hoping to impress your students or push your self-righteous ideas and beliefs upon them.
No matter how vociferously you believe you’re right, or those who disagree with you are evil, don’t do it. Don’t share or opine or wear your politics on your sleeve.

For it drops students further behind and makes them more helpless and dependent. It makes them less confident in themselves and more confused than ever about their place in the universe. It deprives them of learning.
